title: Company Census File - 8 Chicago counties, for-hire, 3-20 PU, registered before 2021
claim: Re-derived the Stage D niche: 3,166 active for-hire carriers with 3-20 power units, registered before 2021, MCS-150 updated 2024+ (Cook 1,564; DuPage 602; Will 414; Lake 206; Kane 166; McHenry 127; Kendall 53; Grundy 34); 3,043 of them hold active MC docket authority. All-status universe with same filters: 7,933 (3,502 active, 4,430 inactive).
excerpt: Query filters: phy_state IL, 8 county codes, classdef contains AUTHORIZED FOR HIRE, power_units 3-20, add_date < 2021-01-01.
limitations: Self-reported MCS-150 data; power units may be stale; inactive records keep last-reported fleet size.

organization: FMCSA Licensing & Insurance (ActPendInsur - All With History)
title: Current BIPD primary insurance filings for the 3,166-carrier niche
claim: 2,750 of 3,166 niche carriers have a current BIPD primary filing. Insurer groups: Progressive (Artisan & Truckers) 14.1%, Great West Casualty 13.0%, Northland/Travelers 12.4%, GEICO (Marine) 8.4%, Sentry 5.5%, Acuity 5.3%, Berkley 4.0%, then a long tail (175 company names). Analyst channel classification (E): ~63% standard agency-appointment carriers, ~27% specialty/fronting/E&S/RRG paper, ~10% direct/captive writers.
excerpt: Counts of current 91X BIPD/Primary filings by name_company, joined on dot_number.
limitations: Filing data shows the insurer, not the retail agent; channel classification of each insurer is our judgement (E), +/-3 pts; a few company names may be mis-grouped.

organization: FMCSA Licensing & Insurance (InsHist - All With History)
title: BIPD filing history for the niche - insurer switching, switch destinations, filing months
claim: Share of established niche carriers whose BIPD primary insurer group changed during the year: 2019 31.8%, 2020 31.9%, 2021 29.8%, 2022 30.1%, 2023 31.4%, 2024 35.7%, 2025 37.0% (1,113 of 3,011). Of 2,366 switches in 2024-25: Progressive 21.4%, GEICO 10.8%, Great West 8.5%, Northland 8.4%, Berkley 4.1%, Sentry 3.6%; ~50% to standard appointment carriers, ~39% to specialty/fronting paper, ~11% to direct writers. Current filing effective months spread evenly (192-289 per calendar month); 1,889 of 2,750 current filings are dated 2024-2026.
excerpt: 30,803 historic filing records for 2,940 niche carriers; switch = new BIPD primary filing from a different insurer group than the prior filing.
limitations: Survivor set (carriers active today); an insurer switch is not the same as an agent switch; 2026 filings partly migrated to FMCSA's Motus datasets; analyst grouping of insurer names (E). Arithmetic is ours.

organization: FMCSA Licensing & Insurance (Revocation - All With History)
title: Authority revocations among established 3-20 PU Chicago for-hire carriers
claim: Carriers (registered pre-2021, 3-20 PU by last report) now inactive whose last common/contract authority revocation fell in the year, as a share of those alive at the start of the year: 2019 5.7%, 2020 3.8%, 2021 2.7%, 2022 3.8%, 2023 5.8%, 2024 4.3%, 2025 2.4%; >90% involuntary (typically insurance lapse).
excerpt: 7,595 revocation records joined to 7,933 all-status census records.
limitations: Lower bound on exits: 1,061 inactive carriers have no revocation record; recent revocations may not yet show as inactive in the census; alive-at-start approximated. Arithmetic is ours (E).

organization: Independent Insurance Agents of Texas (IIAT Advantage)
title: Progressive - market access for IIAT members
claim: Progressive access through this association aggregator requires a Progressive-approved subcode appointment, $1M E&O, portal automation, 2-3 years of agency ownership and P&C experience, a storefront (may be waived), no prior Progressive termination, and agreement to monthly minimum production; commercial auto is among the products.
excerpt: Have at least 2-3 years of agency ownership and P&C experience
limitations: Texas association program; Illinois aggregators may differ; minimum production figures not shown.

title: Small/Mid-Fleet Trucking - ANTU Advantage program
claim: National trucking program on Lancer paper for 1-25 unit risks with no radius restriction, all states except AK, DC, HI, MA, NY; requires two years in business under the current DOT number with two years' verifiable loss experience, 5 years of loss runs, IFTA mileage for 4 quarters, MVRs; distributed through a select group of retail brokers.
excerpt: distributed through a select group of retail brokers
limitations: Commission and retail-broker selection criteria not published.

title: New UG Producer Application with Trucking (rev6 2022; agreement form dated January 2020)
claim: Wholesale GA requires licence copies, E&O of $1,000,000 or more, a separate trucking questionnaire (years in business, years writing commercial auto, total for-hire trucking premium volume, existing trucking GAs, % of book by years of prior insurance); commission 'as approved' by the GA; producer refunds unearned commission on return premium; producer must pay premiums within 30 days of billing whether or not collected; premiums held in trust; producer retains expirations if not delinquent.
excerpt: Producer agrees to pay Union General any and all required premiums
limitations: One California wholesaler's 2020 form; Illinois wholesalers' terms may differ; PDF hosted on the GA's website builder domain.

title: Get a bigger piece of the commission pie
claim: Marketing example: on $500,000 commission a generic network takes $100,000 (20%) while Smart Choice takes $20,000 on Level I carriers; Leadership agents can earn 100% commission. No trucking carriers or start-up criteria stated.
limitations: Marketing; carrier levels, thresholds and Illinois trucking availability not disclosed.

title: Work with Cover Whale - agent page
claim: Live in 46 states; auto liability in 41 states for 1-25 power units at bind (Classes 2-8 incl. hotshots), dashcam or ELD connection required; APD/cargo/NTL/TGL to 75 units; commission described only as competitive; brokers page claims appointment in ~2 days.
limitations: Whether Illinois is among the 41 auto-liability states is not stated; commission % unpublished.

title: Insurance Agency Producer Commission Structure
claim: Producers typically keep 30-90% of agency commission; examples 50% new/40% renewal, 60/40, or 50/50 for both; base-plus-commission for newer producers; unclear renewal ownership on departure is a red flag.
limitations: General explainer by a network that recruits agents; not trucking-specific; no vesting data.

title: 2024 Year End Insurance Agency Valuation Report
claim: Average EBITDA multiple for agencies under $500k revenue 6.8x (from 6.9x in Q3), $500k-$1M 7.55x, $2M-$5M 8.22x; average EBITDA margin <$500k agencies 23.7%, $500k-$1M 24.3%; recommends 8-25% of premium per carrier relationship. Q4-2025 report (2026-02-04): average organic growth 13% in 2025.
excerpt: The average multiple went from 6.9 to 6.8
limitations: Valuation-advisor sample (~270 valuations since 2017), largely standard-lines Ohio/Midwest agencies; not trucking; valuations not completed sales.

organization: IA Magazine (reporting a Liberty Mutual study)
title: Retention Success Happens Beyond Renewal, Says Liberty Mutual Study
claim: Survey of nearly 1,200 independent agency principals and staff: average agency retention rate around 84%.
excerpt: average agency retention rate hovers around 84%
limitations: All lines; self-reported survey; no trucking/commercial split.

title: Business insurance cost for insurance professionals
claim: Median E&O for insurance specialists on Insureon: $65/month ($781/yr), $1M per occurrence/$1M aggregate, $1,000 deductible.
excerpt: sourced from the median cost of small business insurance policies purchased by Insureon customers
limitations: Platform median across agent types; a start-up trucking agency with filings exposure and a compliance-services operation will likely pay more.

organization: ATG Recruiting (division of Hello Logistics Solutions) via career.com
title: Commercial Trucking Insurance Specialist - Independent Contractor (1099), Illinois listing
claim: Illinois-listed, remote, 100% commission 1099 role for licensed P&C agents in commercial trucking; commission based on written premium and retention; trucking experience preferred but not required.
limitations: Job ad; split and book-ownership terms not stated; illustrative earnings figures ambiguous (period not specified).

title: FMCSA issues final rule on non-domiciled CDLs
claim: Final rule scheduled for Federal Register publication 2026-02-13, effective ~2026-03-15; non-domiciled CDL eligibility restricted to H-2A, H-2B or E-2 holders; impact estimated at ~194,000 drivers and possibly more over several years as licences expire.
excerpt: Restricted to H-2A, H-2B, or E-2 holders
limitations: Consultant summary, not the Federal Register text; litigation ongoing (status after May 2026 not confirmed).

title: Progressive Commercial: Agent's Guide 2026
claim: Progressive does not publish commercial commission schedules; rates sit in the agency agreement; appointment via a ForAgentsOnly questionnaire with no commercial-specific detail published.
excerpt: Progressive does not publish commercial commission schedules in any source we opened

title: Trucking market access for a non-specialist agency
claim: A non-trucking agency reports wholesalers declined a risk as a new venture, notes it lacks access to truck markets that do not distribute through brokers and has no trucking volume to promise, and considers referring to a local trucking-specialist agency with direct contracts.
